newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares weak on Middle East peace worries.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares weak on Middle East peace worries.

text.p: Jordanian investor worries over the fate of Middle East peace dampened sentiment in the Amman bourse on Sunday, triggering across-the-board declines, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.35 percent to 152.35 points in shallow turnover worth 158,635 dinars ($224,060).

"There was a psychological effect by political factors weighing down on the market...but the real impact was the lack of liquidity," said Hussam al-Hanbali, head of the Jordanian subsidiary of Arab Banking Corporation's brokerage arm.
The market, traditionally sensitive to political twists and turns in Middle East peace fortunes, has also been hit by a tight monetary policy investors blame for a constant liquidity shortage.
Hanbali also referred to minimal outside buying that was further weakening trade in poor activity overshadowed by the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, when buyers are scarce.
Delays in agreeing this year's trade protocol between Amman and Baghdad also weighed heavily on the market, which had surged last month on Iraq's U.N.-approved oil-for-food deal.

Trucking firm Unified Land Transport, expected to benefit from any increase in shipments to Iraq, was the heaviest traded stock but fell O.02 dinars to 2.10 dinars in trade worth nearly 38,336 dinars.
However some buying in Jordan Cement Factories, which was unchanged at 3.30 dinars, and a handful of other firms kept the market from sliding further.
Union Land Development, the top gainer in the weak market rose 4.76 percent rise to 0.88 dinars.
But overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 21 to six. Shares in eleven companies traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.59 percent to 82.07 points from 82.56 points.
